newsitem.title: TURKEY: Countdown begins for Turkey's ruling Islamists.
newsitem.headline: Countdown begins for Turkey's ruling Islamists.

text.p: Turkey's ruling Islamists on Thursday began a race against the clock to save their crumbling coalition from breaking apart in a row with the secularist army.

Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan held a three-way meeting with a rightist powerbroker and coalition partner Tansu Ciller, whose conservative True Path Party has threatened to pull out of the coalition within a week.

True Path, a pro-Western party, said on Wednesday night it would withdraw from the government if Foreign Minister Ciller was not made prime minister by June 18 under a plan to deflect criticism of the alliance by the powerful army.

"We have openly put forward a solution," Ciller, who was Turkey's first woman prime minister, told reporters after meeting Erbakan. "The solution is democracy, the supremacy of the people's will," she said.
Stocks in Istanbul dived almost three percent on political uncertainty in mid-afternoon trading, brokers said.
The alliance has been hamstrung by disputes over religious activism since the army called in February for a crackdown on Moslem revivalism.
"This government has stopped being effective," the Hurriyet daily on Thursday quoted Ciller as telling her party MPs.
Erbakan is to transfer power to Ciller by the end of this month under a government plan for snap elections to try to resolve the army dispute.

But no date has been fixed for early elections and the coalition allies disagree on the timing of the handover. It would also have to be approved by the president and parliament, where Erbakan now lacks a clear majority.

Far-right leader Muhsin Yazicioglu, whose small Grand Unity Party has eight MPs, joined the talks with Ciller and Erbakan in a possible sign the government was searching for a third coalition partner to boost it in the national assembly.

A leading member of Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party called on Ciller to stay in the 11-month-old alliance. "There is no reason to pull out of the government at the moment," party deputy chairman Ahmet Tekdal told a news conference.
The True Path pullout threat was issued only hours after the military on Wednesday urged ordinary Turks to fight the danger of Islamic activism.

"It is the main duty of every secularist and democratic citizen who loves his country...not to stand neutral and to act against the increasing reactionary threat," General Fevzi Turkeri said at an army briefing for reporters on resurgent Islamism.

The top brass used some of its strongest anti-Islamist language yet at the briefing. Turkeri reminded reporters that the army's role was to protect the country "by force of arms" from domestic and external threats.
The Turkish media took the comment as a warning that the army is willing to use force against the Islamists.
"About the only thing they didn't say was that they are taking over the civilian administration," columnist Mehmet Ali Birand wrote in the Sabah daily.
The military said Iran was playing a role in the spread of Islamist activism in Turkey.
"Iran is providing every kind of support to build a regime in Turkey based on the principles of sharia (Moslem holy law)," Turkeri said.

Erbakan has sought to foster links with Iran since coming to power last June, but the secularist establishment has continued to protest at what it sees as Iranian support for separatist Kurdish rebels fighting in southeast Turkey.
